He should smear them with powders of rice, bamboo, and other materials, using five colors. Thus it is stated in the *Kāraṇa*.

(p.5b, l.1) [He is] dark-complexioned, with his left foot resting on the back of a deer and granting fearlessness; he holds an axe and a supreme sword, and wears bracelets upon his left arm.
I worship the Lord of Umā and Guha, who is accompanied by the Goddess whose other foot is supported by his left arm while she sleeps,
and who is joined by Skanda with his two hands holding a lotus;
he possesses a broad face and eyes, and is endowed with a gentle, graceful, and amorous splendor.
His right hand displays the gesture of granting fearlessness and the boon, and his head is adorned with a crown consisting of the orb of the moon.
With straight limbs and even feet, standing in a posture the color of coral,
holding an axe and a deer in his hands, and seated upon a lotus pedestal.

The equal destruction of the power of Śambhu is described; [he who possesses] a body with eyes of natural form, steady and long, with a blue lotus in his right hand, and a face whose essence is the state of modesty—may there be auspiciousness. [Here ends] the ritual for the fire-sacrifice of pacification (*śāntihoma*). May there be prosperity.
[End of] the procedure for the fire-sacrifice of pacification (*śāntihomavidhiḥ*).
Peace alone is fully described; the rite of the peace-offering (śānti-homa) is now prescribed.
That [rite] is declared to be of two kinds; the superior one is stated first.
In which region are there auspicious hopes? Having prepared a sacrificial mound (*sthaṇḍila*) there in a well-adorned pavilion, one should place a water-pot (*ghaṭa*) in its center—
equipped with a cord, water, a ritual grass-bundle (*kūrca*), cloth, gold, and a lotus.
His limbs were smeared with white sandalwood paste and adorned with mango sprouts.
Having arranged eight water-pots all around, together with the *brahmakūrca* and other [substances],
one should worship the deity named Pāśupata in the center of the jar:
OṂ ŚLĪṂ PAṂ ŚUṂ HUṂ PHAṬ PAŚUPATĀSTRĀYA NAMAḤ | OṂ ŚLĪṂ PĀŚUPADĀSTRAMŪRTAYE NAMAḤ |
Five-faced and ten-eared, with a face turned in every direction and three eyes;
terrifying with its fangs, exceedingly fierce, emitting a great roar, and difficult to conquer.
Adorned with a garland of skulls, having the crescent moon as his crest-ornament,
squint-eyed, wearing great garlands and serpent ornaments, licking [his lips],
possessing a radiance equal to ten million suns, and the crusher of the hosts of obstacles.
With ten fierce arms and terrible weapons, he was exceedingly difficult to conquer.
In the right [hands] are a sword, a bow, a great trident, a noose of fearlessness, and a lasso;
in the left [hands] are a shield, an arrow, a skull-cup, the gesture of granting boons, and a spear.

Having thus meditated upon [the deity] with tawny moustaches, eyebrows, and beard, and likewise with hair of that same color, while reciting the mantra, one should perform the invocation and begin the worship.

Having thus worshipped in the southwest (nairṛta), one should worship the deity with perfumes and other offerings, including the food offering (naivedya), up until the end of the recitation (japa). In front of that, in a square sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) of the size of a cubit, or on a consecrated altar (sthaṇḍila) prepared as before through the five purificatory rites (pañcasaṃskāra), one should invoke the deity Pāśupata along with his limbs (sāṅga), worship him, and offer libations.
[One should offer] fuel-sticks (samidh), clarified butter (ājya), sesame seeds (tila), milk, white dūrvā grass, and sacrificial porridge (caru);
either a thousand times, or half of that, or one hundred and eight times.
One should offer oblations for each [deity] while reciting the mantra and indicating the rite;
the teacher should say, "Perform, perform," for the eightfold pacification of the Blessed One.
Having offered the ten limbs and the ten weapons as oblations, one should satisfy them;
then, having given the final oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) while recollecting the *Pāśupata* weapon-mantra,
and having offered the expiatory oblation (*prāyaścittāhuti*) while recollecting the *Pāśupata* mantra.
Again, having given a full betel leaf and the water offering (arghya), [he should offer it] with his face turned away.
Having gone to one's own abode, one should return and protect the limit of the ritual action;
generating that [deity] every day, one should conceive of him in the form of a weapon.
Having offered the inner oblation (antarbali) and the outer oblation (bahirbali), and having performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana) for the [deity’s] form,
the Guru should pray for the fulfillment of the desired goal, which consists of the state of the deity whose rites have been dedicated.
Then, having released the deity from the pitcher, one should employ him on the twelfth day;
thereafter, one should sprinkle [the area] all around with the waters intended for the installation of that pitcher.

At home, the *śāntihoma* should be performed with sacrificial fuel (*samidh*), clarified butter (*ājya*), and cooked rice (*anna*), without the installation of the ritual water-pot (*kumbha*). It should be conducted for a number of days according to one's capacity. Thus ends the procedure for the *śāntihoma* in the *Kāraṇa-pratiṣṭhā-tantra*. (p.7b, f.2, *diśāhoma*, l.1)
(The Ritual for the Directional Homa:
Next, I shall describe the directional homa, which is declared to be of two kinds.
For the purpose of expiation, one should partake of the musical instruments, the fallen [offerings], and the ointment.
Whether in the *liṅga*, or in an image, or on the pedestal, or in the temple itself; or in a pavilion, a multi-storied building, and so forth; or in the bull, or in the *mūla* [the root-mantra].
When [the damage] increases by half, the wise man should perform the expiation (*prāyaścitta*).

Having constructed a pavilion (*maṇṭapa*) at the front of the temple and a sacrificial altar (*vedi*) in its center, he should prepare a fire-pit (*kuṇḍa*)—either circular or square—measuring one cubit (*hasta*) to the east of that, and adorn it with canopies and other ornaments. Then the preceptor (*guru*), having bathed, performed the ritual of self-protection (*sakalīkṛtya*), and caused the declaration of an auspicious day (*puṇyāha*) to be recited, should prepare the special *arghya* offering and the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*). Having sprinkled [the area], he should sprinkle both the fire-pit and the altar with the *arghya* water.

Having placed jars in the center of the altar—equipped with threads, wrapped in cloth, filled with scented water, and provided with lids made of golden lotuses, *kūrca* grass, sprouts, and coconuts containing the five gems—in the middle, and in the east, south, west, and north; and having also placed the *vardhanī* vessel to the north of the central jar; and having worshipped Śiva in the central jar; [one should worship] in the *vardhanī*: "Oṃ Paṃ Śuṃ Huṃ Phaṭ, obeisance to the form of the Pāśupata weapon.
[It is] lion-faced, with fire-like fangs, possessing a radiance equal to fire, and endowed with upward-pointing crests of flame.
Resembling a black antelope skin, she is endowed with three eyes like round jewels.
Carrying a trident and a hand-drum with their two left hands,
they wear black garments and take delight in the half-moon [crescent] smeared with blood within their mouths.
Having thus meditated upon the Supreme Goddess— adorned on all her limbs with suitable pearl ornaments,
accompanied by the sound of loud laughter, and clothed in a black antelope skin—
one should worship her with perfumes, flowers, and other offerings.

*Oṃ ślīṃ huṃ phaṭ, obeisance to the Pāśupata weapon.* Having thus worshipped [it] along with its limbs (*sāṅga*), one should thereafter worship in the four directions within the pitchers: *Oṃ haḥ, obeisance to the Weapon; Oṃ haḥ, obeisance to the Embodiment of the Weapon.* [He is] four-faced, with blazing hair, possessing a luster like a mass of lightning, having the orb of the moon upon his head, and with four sprout-like hands.

Having thus meditated upon the Weapon of Śiva— which is accompanied by the sound of a thunderbolt, possesses unbearable fear and prowess, has twelve eyes, and likewise holds a spear along with the gestures of granting fearlessness and boons—
one should worship it with perfumes, flowers, and other offerings, using its own mantra.

Having meditated thus, and having worshipped with *oṃ haḥ astrāya huṃ phaṭ*, [one worships] on the right with: *sphura sphura ghora ghora tanurūpa tanurūpa caṭa caṭa pracaṭa pracaṭa kaha kaha vama vama bandha bandha ghātaya ghātaya huṃ phaṭ svāhā*. Having worshipped with these—the Aghorāstra, the seat, the form, and the root mantra—[one worships] in the west: *oṃ ślīṃ paṃ śuṃ huṃ phaṭ*, having worshipped the Pāśupatāstra, the seat, the form, and the root mantra.

O gentle one—*oṃ āṃ īṃ ūṃ*, O Rudrāsthiśṛṅkhalā, *hūṃ*, O Sarvatobhadra, you who carry out the commands of Kuṭilodrava, protect me, O Pratyāṅgirā! *dhāma dhāma jyoti*, bring forth the light! *bhave bhavaḥ*. Protect the immortal god here; truth with the three [steps]; the foot of those free from anger; *lakṣmīṃ namo vaḥ*. What does this Nārīka do? Release him to you, O Mahādeva; O you of good vows, *namaḥ* to me, *svāhā*.

Having thus worshipped the *Pratyaṅgirā* weapon along with the seats (*āsana*), forms (*mūrti*), and root-mantras (*mūla*), and having made this request, one should go to the fire-sanctuary (*pāvakālaya*). Having consecrated the sacrificial pit-fire (*kuṇḍāgni*) as before, and having worshipped Śiva together with his limbs (*sāṅga*) within the heart-lotus of the fire—the root-mantra of the eight Lords of Knowledge (*vidyeśvara*)—one should offer oblations. With *plakṣa*, *udumbara*, *aśvattha*, *vaṭa*, *pālāśa* wood, clarified butter (*ājya*), sesame, *dūrvā* grass, unbroken rice (*akṣata*), and sacrificial porridge (*caru*), they should each offer these substances one hundred or fifty times respectively.

Then, having invoked the weapons (*astras*) into the fire according to the sequence of worship, they should offer oblations (*homa*) one hundred or fifty times with these materials. Afterwards, for the sake of expiation (*prāyaścitta*), having offered one hundred and eight oblations with the *Śivāstra* mantra and having presented the *pūrṇāhuti*, they should present the *caru*. Having established the protective seal (*rakṣādhāna*) and having offered the *arghya*, they perform the confinement of the temple-limbs (*sannirodhana*). Then, having offered the internal oblation (*antarbali*), they pray to the deity—the embodiment of the mantras ending with the invocation—requesting the performance of the ritual.

From its radiance, the performer should perform the offering of ashes. (L. 4) Everything [should be done] in due order. Having bathed the deity with the water from the jar, the Guru should worship it. If that which was performed under the name of the deity is likewise [done] with the waters of the jar, then, aiming at expiation (*prāyaścitta*), the sprinkling (*prokṣaṇa*) is performed. The *diśā-homa* is thus described; it wards off all misfortunes. Thus ends the ritual procedure for the *diśā-homa*.

May there be auspiciousness! Homage to the illustrious one born in the Śara forest. May there be prosperity! Homage to the illustrious Goddess of Speech. May there be prosperity! (p. 9a, root mantra of the eight Lords of Knowledge, l. 1) To Gaṇapati: *oṃ śrīṃ gaṃ gaṇapataye namaḥ*. This is the root mantra. The boon-granting Lord of Obstacles, elephant-faced, son of Umā, with split tusks and ears like winnowing baskets, is the King of Obstacles and possesses eight forms.
For Subrahmaṇya: *oṃ sauṃ śaravaṇabhavaskandāya namaḥ*—this is the root mantra.
Jayanta, Viśākha, Kārttikeya, Ṣaḍānana, Guha, Senāpati, Skanda, and Subrahmaṇya are his eight forms.
Of the Goddess: Oṃ śrīṃ sauṃ saḥ mahāgaurī rudradayite svāhā.
(l.3) Gaurī, Gaṅgā, Durgā, Indrāṇī, and Bhūmidevī.
Sarasvatī, Mahālakṣmī, and Jyeṣṭhā are likewise the Mothers.
For Brahmā: *oṃ hāṃ kaṃ brahmaṇe namaḥ*—this is the root mantra.
*Hrīṃ; Brahmā, Prajāpati, Vedhā, Vidhātṛ, and Pitāmaha.* (l. 4)
She was created by the four-faced Brahmā, who possesses eight forms.
For Viṣṇu: *oṃ hiṃ viṣṇave namaḥ*. This is the root mantra (*mūlamantra*).
Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, Vāsudeva, Aniruddha, Acyuta, Rāma, Nṛsiṃha, and Vāmana.
To Dakṣiṇāmūrti: "Oṃ, salutation to the Blessed One, Dakṣiṇāmūrti; grant me wisdom, svāhā. This is the root mantra.
Sanatkumāra, Sanaka, Sananda, and Sanātana; Agastya, Pulastya, Kauśika, and likewise Kāśyapa.
To Durgā—oṃ duṃ, to Durgā in the south, svāhā!
Durgā, Kātyāyanī, Jayā, Parājitā, Āryā, Bhagavatī, Yantrikā, and likewise Śarvarī. (Verse 7)

One should worship [the deities] named Kāntā in sequence, starting from the east and so forth. For Somāskanda: *oṃ hāṃ vyāmavyāpine śrīkaṇṭhāya namaḥ*. The eight Vidyeśvaras are Ananta and the others. For Kālanigraha: *oṃ jṛṃ haḥ*, the eight Vidyeśvaras are Ananta and the others. For Naṭeśvara: *oṃ sakṣamalavarayūṃ tuṃ purāntabhairavāya nṛttamūrtaye namaḥ*. [The attendants are] Ananta and the others, and the Vidyeśvaras.

Of Caṇḍeśvara: *oṃ hāṃ dhvanicaṇḍeśvarāya huṃ phaṭ namaḥ*. [Indrādi follows. Of Kṣetrapāla: *oṃ śrāṃ kṣīṃ kṣūṃ kṣetrapālakāya namaḥ*; this is the root mantra (*mūlamantra*). Asitāṅga, Ruru, Caṇḍa, Krodha, Unmattabhairava, Kapālī, Bhīṣaṇa, and Saṃhāra are the eight Bhairavas.

Of the Aghorāstra: *oṃ hrīṃ sphura sphura prasphura ghora ghora tanurūpa caṭa caṭa pracaṭa pracaṭa kaḥ kaḥ vama vama ghātaya ghātaya oṃ phaṭ svāhā*. (l. 3) Dreadful, terrifying, formidable, fierce, violent, and bringing fear; Ghora and Ghoratara—these are the forms of the Aghorāstra. Of the Pāśupatāstra: *oṃ ślīṃ paṃ śuṃ huṃ phaṭ pāśupatāstrāya namaḥ*. (l. 4) [The deities] beginning with Indra.

*Oṃ haḥ astrāya phaṭ*—thus is the *Śivāstra*. For the *Pratyaṅgirāstra*: *Oṃ āṃ īṃ raṃ ūṃ rudrāsthiśṛṅkhalāṣṭale hūṃ sarvatobhadre kuṭirudravacanavicāri rakṣa māṃ pratyaṅgire dhāma dhāmajyotijyotiḥ suvas subhuve bhuvaḥ prāśyāmṛto’haṃ satyahantribhidan pādo juṣā lakṣmī namo vaḥ kirikeyaṃ karoti tamo vāñco viśaja mahādeva suvrato namaḥ.*

*Pratyaṅgirā-weapon root mantra*: *svāhā*. *Oṃ saṃ*, O *Pratyaṅgirā* whose tongue is a flame of consumption, whose mouth possesses terrifying fangs! *Oṃ hrīṃ*, homage be to you, *svāhā*. *Kṣurikā-weapon mantra*: *Oṃ kṣuṃ*, for the *Kṣurikā-weapon*, *huṃ phaṭ svāhā*. For *Reṇukā*: *Oṃ hauṃ svāhā*, O Blessed One, *Raktapañcamī*, Goddess *Reṇukā*, burn, burn! Cook, cook! Bring all people under control, bring them under control! *Svāhā*. Jayā and Vijayā, Bhoginī and Mohinī likewise; Malinī and Mālinī, as well as Bhogābhogavatī.
Śivasāvitrī:
We know the one who is the pervasive void; we meditate upon the subtlest of the subtle; may that Rudra inspire us.
Śivagāyatrī:
Oṃ, may we know that Great Lord; may we meditate upon Him whose speech is pure; may that Śiva inspire us. (p. 10a, l. 1) The Astra-gāyatrī:
Oṃ, may we know the Weapon of Śiva; may we meditate upon the Fire of Time; may that Śiva inspire us.
The six-syllable mantra for Sadāśiva:
oṃ hāṃ haṃ sadāśivāya namaḥ. The nine-syllable mantra: [oṃ hāṃ haṃ sadāśivāya namaḥ].
Oṃ hauṃ haṃ saṃ maṃ kṣaṃ raṃ naṃ yaṃ mya?— this is the ten-syllable [mantra].
Oṃ hauṃ saṃ saṃ mūṃ hrūṃ meṃ naṃ maṃ yaṃ— this is [the other] ten.
The Subrahmaṇya Mālā-mantra:
Oṃ śaravaṇabhavāya ṣaṇmukhāya kumārāya kukkuṭadhvajāya huṃ phaṭ svāhā. The Skanda-gāyatrī:
We know the one whose banner is a cock; we meditate upon the one who holds a thunderbolt in his hand; may that Skanda inspire us. For Bhadrakālī:
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ Mahācāmuṇḍī, O Raktacāmuṇḍī, slay, slay! burn, burn! Oṃ svāhā! This is the root mantra.
The *mālāmantra*:

Oṃ hrīṃ Mahācāmuṇḍī Ugracāmuṇḍī oṃ hrīṃ Vīracāmuṇḍīṃ haiṃ Raktacāmuṇḍīṃ hoṃ Khaḍga-śūla-ḍamaruka-kapāla-hastī śrīṃ srīṃ klīṃ Varavarada-Mahācāmuṇḍī svāhā. The eight Śaktis beginning with Brāhmī. For all deities whose [mantras] have not been mentioned, the forms [of the guardians] beginning with Indra [are used]. The eight Śaktis beginning with Brahmā. Salutation to Pālīśvara accompanied by Yogāmbā.
One should perform the previously mentioned ritual procedure together with the procession and the fire-oblation (*homa*).
Having prepared a sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila) at the tip of the liṅga, one should draw an eight-petaled lotus according to the ritual manual.
One should place the *kumbha* on the sacrificial ground (*sthaṇḍila*) and the *vardhanī* to its left,
both equipped with *kūrca* grass, provided with sprouts, and endowed with the nine gems. One should then wrap the *kumbha* in the middle with a cloth.
Combined with water and accompanied by coconut.
Having invoked the Lord who is endowed with all ornaments and accompanied by Kṣelana from the *liṅga*, one should place him within the center of the jar.
Having invoked the Goddess from the pedestal, accompanied by her seed-syllable (*bīja*), [one should place her there].
Adorned with all ornaments and endowed with the act of rinsing the mouth.
Having placed it upon the altar with the Īśāna mantra,
one should then place the *vardhanī* vessel to its left with the *hṛdaya* mantra.
Then, the wise practitioner should place the retinues and the water-pots in their respective positions and worship them with perfumes, flowers, and other offerings.
One should place the Ṛgveda in the eastern quarter, the Yajurveda in the southern,
the Sāmaveda in the western, and likewise the Atharvaveda in the northern.
In this arrangement of locations, one should indeed install them in the west as well.
Specifically regarding the water-pot (*kumbha*), [one should employ] four who have mastered the Vedas;
thus, upon touching the pot, one should likewise mutter the respective mantra.
And just as there is the sprinkling with *śiva* [water] and the formation of the respective seats for the deities (*pīṭhākṛti*).
Likewise, having fashioned it in the shape of a fire-pit (kuṇḍa), one should perform the fire-rite (agnikārya).
Having taken fuel with the *sadyojāta* mantra, one should offer clarified butter (*ājya*) with the root mantra;
having offered the sacrificial porridge (*caru*) with the *aghora* mantra, one should then offer parched grain (*lāja*) with the *tatpuruṣa* mantra.
One should offer mung beans with the heart mantra, and masha beans with the head mantra;
one should offer barley with the eye mantra, and sesame seeds with the vāma-mantra.
One should offer śāli rice with the īśāna-mantra, and wheat with the weapon mantra.
One should offer wild rice with the *śikhā* mantra and roasted barley flour with the *kavaca* mantra.
For the sake of accomplishment through the Pāśupata [mantra], one should offer curd into the primary fire;
then one should offer milk and honey with the ten-syllable mantra.
One should offer molasses with the Heart-mantra and perform the oblation for the fruit of the ten-syllable [mantra].
The most excellent preceptor should perform the fire-oblation (homa) combined with eighteen substances.
Having formed the coconut crest and joined it with the mantra-altar,
one should likewise perform the oblation of the residue (*saṃpātāhuti*) and the oblation of touch (*sparśāhuti*).
Having performed the placement upon the ashes (*bhasmanyāsa*) and so forth, carry out the ritual of totalization (*sakalīkaraṇa*).
One should perform the worship of the pavilion and carry out the fire ritual.
One should sequentially perform the Jaya and other oblations, the re-establishment of the fire, and the Rāṣṭrabhṛt offerings;
then, with the mantra "sviṣṭam agne," one should offer the Pūrṇāhuti while holding it to the head.
Having invoked the Deity from the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), one should then unite Him within the central jar.
But a moment before that time, accompanied by all kinds of musical instruments.
Having recited the *Svastivācana* and the *Śivasaṅkalpa*,
and having lifted the jars and carried them upon his head, he performed a circumambulation of the temple.
Then, having entered the inner sanctum (garbhageha), one should place [the deity] before the liṅga;
having performed the ritual placement of mantras (mantranyāsa) and so forth, as well as the sequence of the placement of the paths (adhvanyāsa).
Having thus honored the preceptor, who is accompanied by the sound of Vedic chanting and joined by various classes of devotees, one should likewise cause a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) to be given.
The satisfaction of the Guru brings about the presence of the Deity; therefore, one should please the Guru in order to make his mind favorable.
Having given cows, land, gold, and other gifts there, he should thoroughly satisfy the Brahmins;
then, after observing the auspicious moment, the astrologer should announce it to the preceptor.
The preceptor, with a perfectly serene mind, standing to the right of the *liṅga*,
should take the seed-syllable from the water-pot and install the Supreme Lord.
And having taken the seed-syllable from the *vardhanī* vessel by means of *manonmanī* as before, [he should proceed].
Having taken the seed-syllable of Vidyeśa, [one should place it] in order from Indra to Īśāna.
One should perform the consecration in that place with the waters contained in the jars;
one should offer the consecration of the divine jar, as well as the mantra-food.
Having especially adorned [the deity] with garments, ornaments, and garlands.
Then, having offered the great oblation, one should maintain the perpetual sacred fire.
Having performed the perpetual festival and so forth, one should carry out everything as before.
One who seeks liberation attains liberation; one who seeks a son obtains a son.
One who seeks wealth acquires wealth; one who seeks victory shall obtain it.
Having attained happiness in this world, he shall in the end attain union (sāyujya).

Thus ends the chapter on the ritual of sprinkling (*saṃprokṣaṇavidhipaṭala*) in the *Aṃśumantatantra*. May there be auspiciousness! May there be success through the compassionate glance of the grace of the venerable Lord Pālīśvara together with the goddess Yogāmbikā. (p. 11b, f. 6a, l.
1) The ritual for binding the protective thread (*rakṣābandhanavidhi*).

Then, regarding the rice grains: *Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Ādhāraśakti*. Regarding the tripod: *Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the principle of the Self (Ātmatattva)*; *Oṃ hiṃ, salutation to the principle of knowledge (Vidyātattva)*; *Oṃ hūṃ, salutation to the principle of Śiva (Śivatattva)*. Having mentally conceived the sixfold seat (*ṣaḍutthāsana*) upon the pedestal: *Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Ananta*; *Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Dharma*; *Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Jñāna*; *Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Vairāgya*; *Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Aiśvarya*; *Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Lotus*. Thus, having worshipped.

In the rice: *astrāya huṃ phaṭ namaḥ*. In the ash-receptacle: *māyātattvāya namaḥ*. In the ashes: *lakulīśvarāya namaḥ*. In the protective thread (*pratisara-sūtra*): *oṃ hāṃ anantāya namaḥ*. In the betel-leaf: *oṃ hāṃ brahmaṇe namaḥ*, *oṃ hāṃ viṣṇave namaḥ*, *oṃ hāṃ rudrāya namaḥ*. In the coconut fruit: *vighneśvarāya namaḥ*. In the east, in the salt: *oṃ hāṃ tatpuruṣavaktrāya namaḥ*. In the south, in the dried cow-dung: [oṃ hāṃ aghoravaktrāya namaḥ].

Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Aghora; in the west, with powdered *rātri* (night-flower), Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Sadyojāta. In the north, with rice, Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Vāmadeva. In the center, with an auspicious thread, one should chant the mantra "Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Īśāna" over the thread. Having performed the offerings of food, betel, and all other services, one should perform the protective binding (*rakṣābandhana*) with the mantra "viśvottāta. Having performed the protection with the "bṛhatsāman," may there be prosperity.

May there be success through the grace and compassionate glance of the venerable Lord Amṛteśvara together with the illustrious Goddess Yogāmbikā. Homage to the illustrious Vāgdevī. May there be prosperity. Homage to the illustrious Dakṣiṇāmūrti. Written by the hand of the Guru Viśvanātha. May there be prosperity. (Folio 12a, line 1) The inner offering and the outer offering—

Then, having prepared two maṇḍalas in the area to the south of oneself: in the first maṇḍala, in the directions starting from the east and ending with the north—namely, in the corners beginning with the northeast—one should offer: *Oṃ hāṃ rudrebhyo namaḥ*; *Oṃ hāṃ mātṛbhyo namaḥ*; *Oṃ hāṃ gaṇebhyo namaḥ*; *Oṃ hāṃ yakṣebhyo namaḥ*; *Oṃ hāṃ gṛhebhyo namaḥ*; *Oṃ hāṃ asurebhyo namaḥ*; *Oṃ hāṃ rākṣasebhyo namaḥ*; *Oṃ hāṃ nāgebhyo namaḥ*.

In the center of the mandala, in the corners of Īśāna, Agni, and Nairṛta: *Oṃ hāṃ nakṣatrebhyo namaḥ*; *Oṃ hāṃ rāśibhyo namaḥ*; *Oṃ hāṃ viśvebhyo namaḥ*. Between Vāyu and Varuṇa: *Oṃ hāṃ kṣetrapālāya namaḥ*. Having thus worshipped and offered the *arghya* ending with *svāhā*, [one proceeds] to the second mandala—in the directions from the East to Īśāna: *Oṃ hāṃ indrāya namaḥ*; *Oṃ hāṃ agnaye namaḥ*; *Oṃ hāṃ yamāya namaḥ*; *Oṃ hāṃ varuṇāya namaḥ*.

Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Vāyu; oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Kubera; oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Īśāna. In the northeast, oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Brahmā; in the southwest, oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Viṣṇu; in the center, oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Nīlalohita. Having thus worshipped them and offered the arghya water, [one should proceed].

Having first offered the *bali* ending with *svāhā* to Rudra and the others, and having given them water for rinsing (*ācamana*), one should likewise offer the *bali* and *ācamana* to Indra and the others. Outside, having worshipped with "Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the crows and others who violate the covenant," and having offered the *bali*, one should offer the *bali* separately with "Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Agni and the others" and "Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to all the planetary deities of the site (*vāstu*"), and after offering the *arghya*, one should dismiss them.

Above the *brahmarandhra*, in the portion of Rudra: homage to Nirodhāśakti; homage to the Śiva-tattva; homage to Śiva, the lord of the Śiva-tattva. At the crown of the head (*mūrdhan*): homage to the Śakti-tattva; homage to Śakti, the lord of the Śakti-tattva. At the throat: Oṃ Hāṃ, homage to the Sadāśiva-tattva; homage to Brahmā, the lord of the Sadāśiva-tattva; homage to the Īśvara-tattva.

Salutation to Ananta, the sovereign lord of the principle of Īśvara. Salutation to the principle of Śuddhavidyā. Salutation to Śambara, the sovereign lord of the principle of Śuddhavidyā. On the left side: salutation to the principle of Māyā. Salutation to Gahaneśa, the sovereign lord of the principle of Māyā. On the right side, in the portion belonging to Viṣṇu—on the chest: salutation to the principle of Kalā. Salutation to the one named Kāla, the sovereign lord of the principle of Kalā. In the heart: salutation to the principle of Niyati.

Homage to the Restrainer, the Lord of the principle of necessity (*niyatitattva*). Homage to the principle of time (*kālatattva*). Homage to the Drop of Knowledge (*jñānabindu*), the Lord of the principle of time. Homage to the principle of knowledge (*vidyātattva*). Homage to the Vedic Wisdom (*vedavijñāna*), the Lord of the principle of knowledge. Homage to the principle of passion (*rāgatattva*). Homage to the Giver of Desire (*kāmadā*), the Lord of the principle of passion. Homage to the principle of the person (*puruṣatattva*). Homage to the Subtle Body (*sūkṣmadeha*), the Lord of the principle of the person. In the belly—homage to the principle of primordial nature (*prakṛtitattva*).

Salutation to Pradhānakāya, the lord of the *prakṛti*-tattva. On the back: salutation to the *guṇa*-tattva. Salutation to Trideha, the lord of the *guṇa*-tattva. Between the navel and the genitals: salutation to the *buddhi*-tattva. Salutation to Buddha, the lord of the *buddhi*-tattva. At the three joints: salutation to the *ahaṃkāra*-tattva. Salutation to Haṃkṛti, the lord of the *ahaṃkāra*-tattva. In the region of Brahmā: salutation to the *manas*-tattva.

Salutation to Saṃkalpa, the presiding deity of the principle of mind (*manas*). Salutation to the principle of hearing (*śrotra*). Salutation to Vyomacāra, the presiding deity of the principle of hearing. Regarding the skin: *Oṃ hāṃ*, salutation to the principle of the skin. Salutation to Sarvāṅga, the presiding deity of the principle of the skin. Regarding the eye: salutation to the principle of the eye. Salutation to Prakāśaka, the presiding deity of the principle of the eye. Regarding the tongue: salutation to the principle of the tongue. Salutation to Mahāvaktra, the presiding deity of the principle of the tongue.

In the nose: *namaḥ* to the principle of the nose (*nāsātattva*). (l. 5) *Namaḥ* to Vilambaka, the lord of the principle of the nose. In the mouth: *namaḥ* to the principle of speech (*vāktattva*). *Namaḥ* to Vibhu, the lord of the principle of speech. *Namaḥ* to the principle of the feet (*pādatattva*). *Namaḥ* to Ramaṇa, the lord of the principle of the feet. (l. 6) In the two hands: *namaḥ* to the principle of the hands (*pāṇitattva*). *Namaḥ* to Sāmagā, the lord of the principle of the hands. In the anus: *namaḥ* to the principle of the anus (*pāyutattva*).

Homage to Tūrṇakṛta, the sovereign of the principle of the anus. At the generative organ—homage to the principle of the generative organ; homage to Ghanānanda, the sovereign of the principle of the generative organ. At the navel—homage to the principle of sound; homage to Sūkṣmanāda, the sovereign of the principle of sound. Homage to the principle of touch; homage to Balavattara, the sovereign of the principle of touch. Homage to the principle of form; homage to Bhānumat, the sovereign of the principle of form.

Homage to the principle of taste (*rasatattva*). (l. 3) Homage to the Lord of the principle of taste, the Water-giver (*jalada*). Homage to the principle of smell (*gandhatattva*). Homage to the Lord of the principle of smell, the Limb of Smell (*gandhāṅga*). In the womb (*yoni*): homage to the principle of space (*ākāśatattva*). (l. 4) Homage to the Lord of the principle of space, the Subtle One (*sūkṣma*). Homage to the principle of wind (*vāyutattva*). Homage to the Lord of the principle of wind, Mātariśvan. In the thighs (*ūrū*): homage to the principle of fire (*agnitattva*). (l. 5) Homage to the Lord of the principle of fire, the Treasury of Splendors (*tviṣāṃ nidhi*).

*Oṃ* homage to the water-principle (*jalatattva*). Homage to Jaleśa, the lord of the water-principle. From below the knees: *Oṃ* homage to the earth-principle (*pṛthivītattva*). Homage to Śrīkaṇṭha, the lord of the earth-principle. Thus ends the section on the principles and their lords (*tattvatattveśvara*). [Next: the section on the forms and their lords (*mūrtimūrtīśvara*). Homage to the form and its lord (*mūrtimūrtīśvara*).

Having thus performed the ritual placement (*vinyāsa*), [one places] the *śivatattva* in the portion of Rudra: *oṃ hūṃ śivatattvāya namaḥ*. *Oṃ hūṃ śivatattvādhipataye namaḥ*. *Rudrāya namaḥ*. In the portion of Viṣṇu: *oṃ hīṃ vidyātattvāya namaḥ*. *Oṃ hīṃ vidyātattvādhipataye viṣṇave namaḥ*. In the portion of Brahmā: *oṃ hāṃ ātmatattvāya namaḥ*. *Oṃ hāṃ ātmatattvādhipataye brahmaṇe namaḥ*. Having thus performed the placement in the sequence starting from the east and ending with the northeast (*aiśāna*).

To Mūrtimūrtīśvara. Oṃ hāṃ lūṃ, obeisance to Kṣmāmūrti. Oṃ hāṃ lūṃ, obeisance to Śarva, the lord of Kṣmāmūrti. Oṃ hāṃ śūṃ, obeisance to Ugra, the lord of Yajamānamūrti. Oṃ hāṃ śūṃ, obeisance to Yajamānamūrti. Oṃ hāṃ śūṃ, obeisance to Ugra, the lord of Yajamānamūrti. Oṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ, obeisance to Arkamūrti. Oṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ, obeisance to Rudra, the lord of Arkamūrti.

Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Pruñjala-mūrti. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Bhava, the lord of Pruñjala-mūrti. Oṃ hāṃ yūṃ, obeisance to Vāyu-mūrti. Oṃ hāṃ yūṃ, obeisance to Īśvara, the lord of Vāyu-mūrti. Oṃ hāṃ sūṃ, obeisance to Indra-mūrti. Oṃ hāṃ sūṃ, obeisance to Mahādeva, the lord of Indra-mūrti. Oṃ hāṃ hūṃ, obeisance to Bhīma, the lord of Kha-mūrti. Thus one should arrange the forms and their presiding deities.

Alternatively—in the five-fold system: in the western, northern, southern, eastern, and northeastern directions: Oṃ hāṃ lūṃ, obeisance to the Earth-form (pṛthivīmūrti). Oṃ hāṃ lūṃ, obeisance to Brahmā, the lord of the Earth-form. Oṃ hāṃ vūṃ, obeisance to the Water-form (jalamūrti). Oṃ hāṃ vūṃ, obeisance to Viṣṇu, the lord of the Water-form. Oṃ hāṃ ruṃ, obeisance to the Fire-form (vahnimūrti). Oṃ hāṃ rūṃ, obeisance to Rudra, the lord of the Fire-form. Oṃ hāṃ yūṃ, obeisance to the Air-form (vāyumūrti).

Oṃ hāṃ yūṃ, salutation to Īśvara, the lord of the wind-form. Oṃ hāṃ hūṃ, salutation to the ether-form. Oṃ hāṃ hūṃ, salutation to Sadāśiva, the lord of the ether-form. Having thus performed the placement (*nyāsa*) for each section, one should restrain [the breath].
Following the teacher’s instruction, one should slowly recite the mantra from the *kanda* and other centers;
it consists of the power of resonance (*nāda-śakti*), is subtle, and spreads through the resonance of the *khaṇṭā*.
Through the yoga of abandoning the causes, it has emerged from the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*),
possessing the brilliance of a thousand suns and equal to ten million flashes of lightning.
With a canopy of shimmering rays illuminating the quarters of space, and having mentally dissolved the mantra, [he attains] bliss in the presence of the Sage...
(p.16a, l.1). Having brought down from the *dvādaśānta* the partless (*niṣkala*) and all-pervading Śiva.
Endowed with thirty-eight rays and blazing with a thousand beams of light.
Having meditated upon the effulgent form, which consists of all powers and is complete with its limbs, resembling a line of bees,
he brought it from the forehead to the door of the throat-center.
Having meditated upon [the deity] emerging from the *suṣumnā*, shimmering like a star, one should place it,
extending through the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*) and pervading the entire body.
O God, this is the "Installation of Life" (*jīvanyāsa*), which accomplishes all purposes within the *liṅga*.
Establishment, placement, confinement, and veiling;
(l.4) showing [the deity] with a mudrā, water for the feet, water for rinsing the mouth, the arghya offering, and flowers—
having consecrated [the deity] with these and worshipped it, one likewise covers it with a cloth.
One should construct three enclosures outside with ashes, *darbha* grass, and sesame seeds. On the pedestal (*piṇḍikā*), beginning from the stalk (*nāla*):

"Oṃ hīṃ, obeisance to the Śakti-tattva. Oṃ hīṃ, obeisance to Śakti, the sovereign of the Śakti-tattva. On the upper part above the neck of the pedestal, having placed a flower garland and a protective cord (*pratisara*) upon the stalk portion for the purpose of conceptualizing the three sections: "Oṃ hūṃ, obeisance to the Śiva-tattva. Oṃ hūṃ, obeisance to Icchā-śakti, the sovereign of the Śiva-tattva. At the neck of the pedestal: "Oṃ hiṃ, obeisance to the Vidyā-tattva."

Oṃ hiṃ, obeisance to the Power of Knowledge (*jñānaśakti*), the sovereign of the principle of knowledge (*vidyātattva*). In the region below the throat: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the principle of the self (*ātmatattva*). Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Power of Action (*kriyāśakti*), the sovereign of the principle of the self. Then, in the respective directions starting from the east: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the form of earth (*kṣmāmūrti*). Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Dhārikā, the sovereign of the form of earth. Obeisance to the form of fire (*agnimūrti*). Obeisance to Dīptimatī, the sovereign of the form of fire.

Salutation to the form of the Sacrificer (*yajamāna-mūrti*). Salutation to Ugrā, the presiding deity of the form of the Sacrificer. Salutation to the form of the Sun (*arka-mūrti*). Salutation to Jyotsnā, the presiding deity of the form of the Sun. Salutation to the form of Water (*jala-mūrti*). Salutation to Cetanā, the presiding deity of the form of Water. Salutation to the form of Wind (*vāyu-mūrti*). Salutation to Balotkaṭā, the presiding deity of the form of Wind. Salutation to the form of the Moon (*indu-mūrti*). Salutation to Dhātrī, the presiding deity of the form of the Moon. Salutation to the form of Space (*ākāśa-mūrti*).

Salutation to the one who is the presiding deity of the form of space (*ākāśa-mūrti*), who is to be meditated upon. Or else, according to the five-fold division: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the form of earth (*pṛthivī-mūrti*). Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Vāmaśakti, the presiding deity of the form of earth. Salutation to the form of water (*jala-mūrti*). Salutation to Yogaśakti, the presiding deity of the form of water. Salutation to the form of fire (*vahni-mūrti*). Salutation to Kriyāśakti, the presiding deity of the form of fire. Salutation to the form of air (*vāyu-mūrti*). Salutation to Jñānaśakti, the presiding deity of the form of air.

"Salutation to the one whose form is space (*ākāśamūrti*); salutation to the power of will (*icchāśakti*), the presiding deity of the form of space. Having thus performed the ritual placement (*vinyāsa*) and having restrained [the breath], [one should recite]: "Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to the power of action (*kriyāśakti*). Having performed the ritual placement of the power of action, [one should recite]: "Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ saṃ, Mahāgaurī, beloved of Rudra, svāhā! Having uttered this up to the end of the *śakti*, having invoked [the deity], established [her], and restrained [the breath], one should likewise perform the ritual placement on the bull (*vṛṣabha*). [Reciting]: "Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to the bull," one should invoke [him] and restrain [the breath].

Having likewise placed [the deity] upon the foundation stone (*ādhāraśilā*) with [the mantra]: *oṃ sūṃ ādhāraśaktaye namaḥ* and *oṃ hrīṃ vā*, having thus invoked [her], one should construct three enclosures outside with their ashes, *darbha* grass, and sesame seeds. Thus, for the practitioner, one should install the image (*mūrti*) together with its presiding lord (*mūrtīśvara*), as well as the eight Lords of Knowledge (*aṣṭavidyeśvara*). This concludes the installation of the image and its presiding lord. One should worship the images beginning with Nivṛtti and the presiding lords of the forms beginning with Sadyojāta, starting from the west and ending in the northeast (*īśāna*).

Having cooked the sacrificial oblation (*caru*) according to the previously mentioned procedure and having offered it into each of the fire-pits (*kuṇḍa*), one should empower the peace-pitchers (*śāntikumbha*) by reciting the *astreṇa* mantra a hundred times and performing the *sampāta* oblations. Then, having projected the Supreme Lord (*parameśvara*) into the center of the pit, the four digits (*kalā*) beginning with Nivṛtti upon the girdles, the power of action (*kriyā-śakti*) in the navel, and the Sound (*nāda*) upon the lip, one should effect the union of the channels (*nāḍī-sandhāna*) between Śiva residing in the pitcher, on the sacrificial ground, and in the fire, together with one's own self.
The channel, resembling a fine spider’s thread, has emerged forth with joy.
Entering with falsehood and departing with joy.

I contemplate [the deity] entering while the self has not yet arisen; otherwise, having offered three oblations into the *kuṇḍa* for the purpose of that union—having worshipped with "Oṃ Hāṃ, obeisance to Ādhāraśakti" and offered three oblations, and having worshipped the *ātmatattva* and its Lord, offering three oblations to each—the Guru then [offers]: "Oṃ Hāṃ, obeisance to Yakṣmāmūrti; obeisance to Śarva, the lord of Kṣmāmūrti; obeisance to Vahnimūrti; obeisance to Paśupati, the lord of Vahnimūrti; obeisance to Yajamānamūrti."

Having worshipped [them] with the words: "Homage to the fierce one, the presiding lord of the form of the sacrificer; homage to the Sun-form; homage to Rudra, the presiding lord of the Sun-form; homage to the Water-form; homage to Bhava, the presiding lord of the Water-form; homage to the Wind-form; homage to Īśvara, the presiding lord of the Wind-form; homage to the Moon-form; homage to Mahādeva, the presiding lord of the Moon-form; homage to the Space-form; homage to Bhīma, the presiding lord of the Space-form."

Having offered three oblations for each [deity] ending with *svāhā*, in the fivefold system: *oṃ hāṃ* homage to the Earth-form (*pṛthivīmūrti*); homage to Brahmā, the presiding lord of the Earth-form; homage to the Water-form; homage to Viṣṇu, the presiding lord of the Water-form; homage to Viṣṇu, the presiding lord of the Air-form; homage to Īśvara; homage to the Space-form; homage to Sadāśiva, the presiding lord of the Space-form. Having thus worshipped them:

Having offered three oblations ending with "svāhā," one should offer the root mantra, the Brahma-mantras, and the limb-mantras (aṅga-mantras) each one hundred, one thousand, or half [of that], together with the final full oblation (pūrṇāhuti). According to the availability of materials and time, one may offer one hundred oblations with the root mantra. Having offered the Brahma-mantras and the limb-mantras one thousand, half, or one hundred times—equivalent to a tenth part—and having performed the final full oblation, the preceptor then takes the peace-vessel (śāntikumbha), goes near the liṅga, and sprinkles Śiva with the water from the peace-vessel.

Having touched the Brahmā-aṅga with the root mantra and the roots of *kuśa* grass, and having performed the recitation (*japa*) the number of times equal to the *homa* count, the Guru should thereafter effect their presence (*sannidhi*) by means of the heart-mantra alone, conceal them with the armor-mantra (*varman*), and having restrained them, he should cause the presiding deity of the principles (*tattvādhipa*) to hear the command: "O Brahman, presiding deity of the self-principle (*ātmatattva*), as long as faults have arisen, this *liṅga* belongs to you; you must remain right here through your presence. Thus [he says].

"Oṃ hāṃ hiṃ, obeisance to the *ātmatattva* and the *vidyātattva*. Thus one should worship up to the end of *māyā* by pronouncing the mantras ending in the *bindu*. Having worshipped with: "Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the *ātmatattva* and the *vidyātattva*, to Brahmā and Viṣṇu," [one continues]: "Oṃ lūṃ lūṃ, obeisance to the two forms of Earth (*kṣmāmūrti*). "Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the two Lords of the Earth-forms (*kṣmāmūrtyadhipa*), to Śarva and Abja. "Oṃ rūṃ rūṃ, obeisance to the two forms of Fire (*vahnimūrti*)."

Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the two Paśupatis, the lords of the Fire-form. Oṃ śrūṃ śrūṃ, obeisance to the two [deities] of the Sacrificer-form. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the two Ugras, the lords of the Sacrificer-form. Oṃ ṣūṃ ṣūṃ, obeisance to the two [deities] of the Sun-form. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the two Rudras, the lords of the Sun-form. Oṃ vūṃ vūṃ, obeisance to the two [deities] of the Water-form. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the two Bhavas, the lords of the Water-form.

Oṃ yūṃ yūṃ, salutation to the two forms of Vāyu. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two Īśānas, the presiding lords of the form of Vāyu. Oṃ sūṃ sūṃ, salutation to the two forms of Indra. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two Mahādevas, the presiding lords of the form of Indra. Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ, salutation to the two forms of Ākāśa. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two Bhīmas, the presiding lords of the form of Ākāśa. Thus one should offer [the oblation]. In the five-fold system: Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two forms of Pṛthivī.

Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two Brahmās, the lords of the earth-forms. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two [deities] of the water-forms. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two Viṣṇūs, the lords of the water-forms. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two [deities] of the fire-forms. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two Rudras, the lords of the fire-forms. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two [deities] of the wind-forms. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two Īśvaras, the lords of the wind-forms.

*Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutations to the two whose forms are space.* *Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutations to Sadāśiva and [his consort], the lords of the two whose forms are space.* Having thus worshipped, one should go to the vicinity of the *kuṇḍa*, worship there, and offer five oblations with the root mantra for the purpose of their union: *Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutations to the two principles of knowledge (*vidyā-tattva*).* *Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutations to Viṣṇu and [his consort], the lords of the principle of knowledge.* Having thus worshipped and caused them to become present, one should offer three oblations to each.

One should perform the *saṃhitā*-oblation as before. Afterwards, having gone near the *liṅga*, and having first sprinkled it with water from the peace-vessel (*śāntikumbha*) as before, one should touch the portion belonging to Viṣṇu with the middle part of *kuśa* grass while reciting the *mūla-mantra*. Having performed the recitation (*japa*) according to the number of oblations and having sprinkled it with the water of peace, one should perform the *avaguṇṭhana* and *nirodhana* rites while remaining ever attentive. Then, one should announce the command to Viṣṇu: "O Viṣṇu, in the state of the *vidyā-tattva*, [whatever has arisen] through the faults..."

"O Liṅga, you must remain right here in my presence. Then, having worshipped with the recitation ending in the *bindu* and ending in the *nāda*: "Oṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ, salutation to the two principles of Vidyā and Śiva," and having worshipped: "Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to Viṣṇu and Rudra, the lords of the two principles of Vidyā and Śiva," and [having worshipped]: "Oṃ lūṃ lūṃ, salutation to Kṣmā and Mūrti; Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two Śarvas, the lords of Kṣmā and Mūrti."

Oṃ rūṃ rūṃ, salutations to the two forms of Fire. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutations to the two Pashupati lords of the two forms of Fire. Oṃ śūṃ śūṃ, salutations to the two forms of the Sacrificer. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutations to the two Ugra lords of the two forms of the Sacrificer. Oṃ ṣūṃ ṣūṃ, salutations to the two forms of the Sun. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutations to the two Rudra lords of the two forms of the Sun. Oṃ vūṃ vūṃ, salutations to the two forms of Water.

Oṃ vavūṃ vūṃ, homage to the two Bhavas, lords of the water-forms. Oṃ yūṃ yūṃ, homage to the two [deities] of the wind-forms. Oṃ hāṃ oṃ hāṃ, homage to the two Īśānas, lords of the wind-forms. Oṃ sūṃ sūṃ, homage to the two [deities] of the moon-forms. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, homage to the two Mahādevas, lords of the moon-forms. Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ, homage to the two [deities] of the space-forms. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, homage to the two Bhīmas, lords of the space-forms.

Having thus performed the worship, in the five-fold system (*pañcapakṣa*): Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the two forms of Earth (*pṛthivīmūrti*). Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the two Brahmās, the presiding lords of the form of Earth (*pṛthivīmūrtyadhipa*). Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the two forms of Water (*jalamūrti*). Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the two Viṣṇūs, the presiding lords of the form of Water (*jalamūrtyadhipa*). Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the two forms of Fire (*vahnimūrti*). Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the two Rudras, the presiding lords of the form of Fire (*vahnimūrtyadhipa*). Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the two forms of Wind (*vāyumūrti*).

Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two lords, Īśvaras, who are the presiding deities of the wind-forms. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two [deities] of the space-forms. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two Sadāśivas, who are the presiding deities of the space-forms. Thus one should perform the conjunction (*saṃdhāna*). The guardians of the forms (*mūrtipās*) should also perform the conjunction of their respective forms. Then, having gone to the vicinity of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*), and having performed worship, they should offer oblations for the sake of the conjunction.

Then, having worshipped the Śivatattva and its lord Rudra according to the previous procedure by means of the sequence of union (*sandhāna*), having caused them to be present and worshipped them, and having offered three oblations for each with the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*), one should perform the *saṃhitā-homa* as before. Afterwards, having gone near the liṅga, having sprinkled it with water from the *śānti-kumbha*, and having touched the portion belonging to Rudra with the tip of a *kuśa* blade while reciting the root mantra, one should perform the recitation (*japa*) according to the number of oblations and sprinkle it again with the *śānti* water.

Having performed the binding and sealing with the *hṛdaya-mantra* and having restrained [the breath], one should proclaim the command to Rudra: "O Lord Rudra-Śiva, you are known; O Lord, you must remain here in this state of the Śiva-tattva for as long as any defect has arisen in the *liṅga*. Having thus informed him, the officiant, who is the lord of the forms beginning with Earth, should worship the forms beginning with Earth and their respective lords according to the previous sequence of union. Then, for the sake of purifying the *puṇḍrikā*, he should go to the vicinity of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*).

Having performed worship as before: *Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the principle of the self (ātmatattva)*; *Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the creative power (kriyāśakti), the sovereign of the principle of the self*—having thus worshipped in the fire and offered three oblations: *Oṃ hauṃ, obeisance to the form of Earth (kṣmāmūrti)*; *obeisance to Dhārikā, the sovereign of the form of Earth*; *obeisance to the form of Fire (vahnimūrti)*; *obeisance to Dīptimatī, the sovereign of the form of Fire*; *obeisance to the form of the Sacrificer (yajamānamūrti)*; *obeisance to Ugrā, the sovereign of the form of the Sacrificer*; *obeisance to the form of the Sun (arkamūrti)*.

Salutation to Jyotsnā, the presiding deity of the solar form; salutation to the water-form; salutation to Cetanā, the presiding deity of the water-form; salutation to the wind-form; salutation to Balotkaṭā, the presiding deity of the wind-form; salutation to the Indra-form; salutation to Dhātrī, the presiding deity of the Indra-form; *oṃ hāṃ*, salutation to the ether-form; *oṃ hāṃ*, salutation to Vidyā, the presiding deity of the ether-form. Having worshipped thus and offered three oblations for each [deity], [one should proceed].

In the fivefold division: *oṃ hāṃ* obeisance to the Earth-form; *oṃ hāṃ* obeisance to Vāmā, the presiding deity of the Earth-form. Obeisance to the Water-form; obeisance to Jyeṣṭhā, the presiding deity of the Water-form. Obeisance to the Fire-form; obeisance to Kriyā, the presiding deity of the Fire-form. Obeisance to the Air-form; obeisance to Jñānī, the presiding deity of the Air-form. Obeisance to the Space-form; obeisance to Icchā, the presiding deity of the Space-form. Having thus worshipped them:

One should offer three oblations for each [deity]. One should then offer one hundred oblations, together with a final full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*), reciting: *oṃ hrīṃ kriyāśaktaye svāhā*. Then the Guru, taking the *śāntikumbha* (peace-pitcher), goes near the pedestal (*pīṭha*). Having sprinkled the pedestal with the water from the *śāntikumbha*, he touches the base of the pedestal with the root of a *kuśa* blade while reciting the root mantra. Having performed the recitation (*japa*) as many times as the number of oblations offered, and having sprinkled it again with the water from the *śāntikumbha*, the Guru subsequently performs their unification (*saridhi*) by means of his own heart.

Having enveloped [the deity] with armor and restrained [it], one should cause the Lord of Principles (*tattvādhipa*) to hear the command: "O Lord of Principles, as long as the seat (*pīṭha*) arises from defects, you must remain right here through your presence. *Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the Self-principle (*ātmatattva*) and the Knowledge-principle (*vidyātattva*). Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Lords of the Self-principle and the Knowledge-principle, namely Action (*kriyā*) and Knowledge (*jñāna*).* Having thus worshipped, [one says]: *Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Earth (*kṣmā*) and Form (*mūrti*).*

Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, homage to the two presiding deities of the earth-form (*kṣmāmūrti*), the two Sustainers (*dhārikā*). Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, homage to the two fire-forms (*vahnimūrti*). Homage to the two presiding deities of the fire-form, the two Radiant Ones (*dīptimatī*). Homage to the two sacrificer-forms (*yajamānamūrti*). Homage to the two presiding deities of the sacrificer-form, the two Fierce Ones (*ugrā*). Homage to the two sun-forms (*arkamūrti*). Homage to the two presiding deities of the sun-form, the two Moonlight Ones (*jyotsnā*). Homage to the two water-forms (*jalamūrti*).

Salutation to the two conscious beings who are the lords of the water-forms. Salutation to the two wind-forms. Salutation to the two lords of the wind-forms, Balotkaṭa and [his consort]. Salutation to the two moon-forms. Salutation to the two lords of the moon-forms, Dhārikā and [her consort]. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two ether-forms. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two lords of the ether-forms, Vidyā and [her consort]. Thus one should join [the mantras]. In the five-fold system: Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two earth-forms.

Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two Vāmās, the presiding deities of the earth-form; salutation to the two Moon-forms; salutation to the two Dhārikās, the presiding deities of the moon-form. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two Space-forms; Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two Icchās, the presiding deities of the space-form. Having thus performed the conjunction (*sandhāna*), having gone to the vicinity of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) and worshipped [the deities], they should offer oblations for the sake of their presence (*sannidhāna*). Then, having worshipped the principle of knowledge (*vidyātattva*), its sovereign goddess, and the Knower (*jñānin*).

Having brought [the materials] near, and having offered three oblations for each with [mantras] ending in *svāhā*, one should offer a hundred oblations along with the final full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) using the root-mantra of Śakti as before. Afterwards, having gone near the pedestal (*pīṭha*), and having first sprinkled it with water from the peace-vessel (*śāntikumbha*) as before, one should touch the central part of the pedestal with the middle of a *kuśa* blade while reciting the root-mantra. Having performed the recitation [of the mantra] the same number of times as the oblations, and having sprinkled it with the water of peace, one should perform the veiling (*avakuṇṭhana*) and the sealing (*nirodhana*) with the Heart-mantra.
Then, one should cause the presiding lord of the power of knowledge (*jñānaśakti*) to hear the command.

"The knower [should understand] that as long as there exists a sacred seat (pīṭha) arising from defects within the Lord of the Principle of Knowledge (vidyātattva), he must remain right here by virtue of his presence. Thus it is said.

Then—having worshipped with: "Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ, obeisance to the *vidyātattva* and *śivatattva*. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the *vidyātattva* and *śivatattva*, and to Knowledge (*jñāna*) and Will (*icchā*)," and having performed the conjunction (*sandhāna*) as before for the deities and their forms beginning with Earth (*kṣmā*), and having gone to the vicinity of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) and worshipped, they should offer oblations for the sake of conjunction. Then, having worshipped the Sovereign Lady (*īśvarī*) who terminates in the *śivatattva*, and the Power of Will (*icchāśakti*), and having caused them to become present (*sannidhāpya*).

Having offered three oblations for each [deity], one should perform the fire sacrifice (*homa*) one hundred times with the root mantra, including the final full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*). Then, having gone near the pedestal (*pīṭha*), and having sprinkled it with water from the *śānti*-vessel, one should touch the front part of the pedestal with the tip of a *kuśa* blade while reciting the root mantra. Having performed the recitation (*japa*) according to the number of oblations, and having sprinkled it again with the *śānti*-water, one should perform the consecration (*sannidhi*) with the *hṛdaya*-mantra, perform the veiling (*avakuṇṭhana*), and effect the confinement (*niruddha*). One should then cause the presiding deity of the principles (*tattvādhipa*) to hear the command:
"O Power of Knowledge (*jñānaśakti*), you have known the Śiva-principle as the controller."
"The Goddess should remain here as long as there arises any fault. Thus [it is said]. (l. 8)

In this same manner, having performed everything upon the foundation stone (*ādhāraśilā*) as on the pedestal (*pīṭha*), at the time of the fire-oblation (*homa*), one should offer oblations with: *oṃ sūṃ ādhāraśaktyai svāhā*. Having also performed the recitation (*japa*), one should effect the confinement (*nirodha*). Regarding the bull (*vṛṣabha*) as well, it is done as before. Having gone near the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*), and having performed the rites beginning with the deposition of the Foundation Power (*ādhāraśakti-nyāsa*), followed by the worship and offering of oblations to the Principles (*tattva*), the Lords of the Principles (*tattvādhipa*), the Embodiments (*mūrti*), and the Lords of the Embodiments (*mūrtīśvara*), one should offer one hundred oblations along with the final full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) with: *oṃ hrīṃ vṛṣabhāya svāhā*. Then, having gone near that [bull], [one should proceed].

Having performed the sprinkling with the water of pacification (*śāntyambhas*), the touching of the roots, middle, and tips of the *kuśa* grass, and the joining of the two tattvas by means of recitation (*japa*), he should go [to the fire], offer oblations, and having returned, perform everything as before. Then, for the purpose of removing defects such as those at the base of the *liṅga*, he should offer one hundred oblations each with the *Aghora* mantra of Śiva, accompanied by a full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*). Having offered the sacrificial porridge (*caru*) and performed the final full oblation, he should provide water for sipping (*ācamana*), betel, and so forth. Having confined Śiva, offered the *vyāhṛti* oblations, presented the inner offering (*antarbali*), and performed the salutation to the ears (*śrotravandana*).
Having made [the offering] savory and having gone into the presence of Śiva, [he says] at the right ear of Śiva: "O Lord,

O you who are affectionate toward devotees, whatever action has been performed by me— whether deficient or excessive— in the three aspects beginning with Brahmā, through knowledge or through delusion."
"May all that be complete here in this sacrifice through your grace.
Oṃ, salutations to you, the Blessed One; O Rudra, the fierce one, let there be salutations to you.
Whether the rite be complete or incomplete, may it be accepted as fulfilled according to my own capacity. Having thus made this request:

Having deposited the power of knowledge (*jñānaśakti*), he should restrain [the breath]. Having gone near the pedestal (*pīṭha*), he should inform [the deity]: "O Blessed One, by your grace, may the cessation of my ritual action in all three parts reach completion. Having informed [her] with "Oṃ hrīṃ Śaṅkarī, fulfill, fulfill, svāhā," he should deposit the power of action (*kriyāśakti*) and restrain [the breath]. Regarding the Brahma-stone (*brahmaśilā*) as well, having informed [her]: "May all the ritual action be fulfilled; let it be accepted."

Having performed the ritual placement (*vinyāsa*) of the *ādhāraśakti* with the mantra "Oṃ sūṃ, obeisance to the *ādhāraśakti*," one should restrain [the breath]. Having also informed the bull [of this], one should restrain the bull with the mantra "Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the Bull" (*vṛṣabha*). [This should be done] with fire oblations (*homa*), the sounding of the Vedas and other scriptures, and great festivals of dance and song, out of devotion for seven nights, five nights, or three nights.
One should perform the preliminary consecration (adhivāsana) of the deity for one night below [the altar];
every day, one hundred oblations each should be offered with their respective mantras.
One should present the worship of the Śiva-pitcher and other vessels, as well as the offering to the quarters (*digbali*).

Together with the image-keepers (*mūrtipas*), the preceptor (*ācārya*) should drink the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*) and so forth. Thus, in the case of a multi-day rite, according to the *Kriyākāṇḍa*: "The mantrin should sleep during the middle portion [of the night], and immediately thereafter, together with the image-keepers. This concludes the procedure for the preliminary consecration (*adhivāsana*) in the *Śivālayanirmāṇadīpikā*.

Then, having risen at dawn and performed his daily rites, the Guru—having performed the worship of the Sun and the door-keepers, the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*), the internal sacrifice (*antaryāga*), the consecration of the substances for the special *arghya* offering, the formation of the *śivahasta*, the worship of the *śivabhāva*, the *lokapālas*, the *śivakumbha*, the *vardhanī*, Gaṇapati, the Guru, and the sacrificial mound (*sthaṇḍila*)—and having received permission, while uttering the weapon-mantra ending in *huṃ phaṭ*, went to the temple. Having driven away the obstacles and sprinkled [the area] with the weapon-mantra, he worshipped Śiva with the eightfold flower-offering (*aṣṭapuṣpikā*).

Having worshipped with "Oṃ sūṃ, obeisance to Ādhāraśakti," and having recited and worshipped with "Oṃ, obeisance to you, O pervasive one, firm, immovable, and stable; Laṃ Hrīṃ Laṃ Svāhā," one should inform her: "You alone are the Supreme Śakti; you alone are the sustainer of the seat. By the command of Śiva, O Goddess, you must remain here perpetually. Then, having gone near the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) and sprinkled it with the weapon-mantra (*astramantra*), one should worship Brahmā and the others, as well as Indra and the other guardians of the world (*lokapāla*), upon the girdles (*mekhalā*).

Having consecrated the *sṛk* and *sruva* ladles with clarified butter as before, and having offered the full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*), one should worship Śiva in the fire as previously described. Having performed the libation for the mantras, one should offer a hundred oblations each, accompanied by the full oblation, using the sword-mantra of Śiva. Then, having attained the presence of Śiva and saying "Become firm," once the *liṅga* has become stable, one should raise it from the head by one cubit. Having meditated upon the all-pervading Lord who possesses all forms, one should utter the *prāsāda* mantra and lead [the deity] down to the end of the Power (*śakti*) within the sphere of the partless (*niṣkala*). One should then install the partless form within that image.

In reality, that which is fashioned by the power of action (kriyā-śakti) and established by the power of knowledge (jñāna-śakti) must exist in its true nature as the object of knowledge (jñeya) and that which is supported (ādheya).
Having invoked [the deity] and visualized them as being face-to-face, and having granted presence and confinement,
one should offer water for the feet and the facial arghya, and worship with a flower alone.

"Oṃ hrīṃ hauṃ, salutations to Kriyāśakti and Śiva. (L. 7) Having thus worshipped both the pedestal (*pīṭha*) and the *liṅga* with the *liṅgamudrā*, for one seeking liberation (*mumukṣu*), [the procedure is]: "Oṃ hauṃ hrīṃ, salutations to Śiva and Śakti. Having touched the *liṅga* and the pedestal with this, one should deposit the six paths (*adhvaṣaṭka*). Having worshipped in this manner, one should worship the forms (*mūrti*) known as Earth, Fire, Sacrificer, Sun, Water, Wind, Moon, and Space, and those named Śarva, Paśupati, Ugra, Rudra, Bhava, Īśāna, Mahādeva, and Bhīma. [This is done] according to the five-fold system.

Having projected the deities known as the forms of earth, water, fire, air, and ether, and the lords of the forms known as Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara, and Sadāśiva; having projected the mantras beginning with Ādhāraśakti and ending with Śakti upon the pedestal (pīṭha); having projected the form [of the deity] upon the liṅga according to the sequence of Brahmā’s parts and performed the deposition of the thirty-eight kalās; having brought about the body of knowledge (vidyādeha); having performed another deposition on the eyes, invoked [the deity] with the root mantra, established it, made it present, restrained it, and deposited the limbs.

Having performed the offerings of water for the feet (*pādya*), water for sipping (*ācamana*), the respectful offering (*arghya*), and flowers; having applied [the mantra] *oṃ hauṃ sauṃ jñānaśaktaye namaḥ* to the *liṅga*; having applied *oṃ hrīṃ kriyāśaktaye namaḥ* to the pedestal (*pīṭha*); having performed the act of confinement (*nirodha*); having offered incense and lamps; having bathed [the deity] with the *śānti*-water and the water from the conch; having anointed [it] all over with sandalwood paste and other substances; and having clothed [it] in a garment.

Having adorned [the deity] with necklaces, earrings, crowns, sacred threads, silken cloths, and so forth; having offered incense and lamps; having worshipped the limbs of the *laya* (dissolution); having fully worshipped the limbs of enjoyment (*bhoga*); having worshipped the remainder up to the fifth enclosure (*pañcamāvaraṇa*) and offered the water for honor (*arghya*); having presented the food offering (*naivedya*) and other items; having gratified [the deity] with incense, lamps, the *rātrika* lamp, mirrors, parasols, fly-whisks, songs, dances, and so on; and having performed the recitation (*japa*) and the formal announcement (*nivedana*), one should then address a request to Śiva.

"O Lord, you should remain here in this temple at your own will, together with the lords of mantras and the guardians of the forms, for as long as the moon, sun, and stars endure. Having thus petitioned and obtained his permission, having prostrated with eight limbs and gone outside, having worshipped the bull with the heart-mantra or the *praṇava*, he goes to the vicinity of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*).

For the sake of pacification, the Guru, having offered one hundred oblations with the *mṛtyuñjaya* mantras using the leaves of the *arka*, *palāśa*, *khadira*, *apāmārga*, *aśvattha*, *udumbara*, *śamī*, *dūrvā*, and *kuśa*, or with sesame seeds; or with milk-rice (*pāyasa*) consecrated by the *mṛtyuñjita* mantra, as well as with the root-mantra (*mūlamantra*) and the two *umā* mantras; and for the sake of atonement (*prāyaścitta*), having offered one hundred oblations with either the root-mantra or the *aghora* mantra, having presented the sacrificial porridge (*caru*), having given the final full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*), and having provided water for sipping (*ācamana*) and so forth, he should perform the ritual confinement (*nirudhya*).

Having offered oblations with the *bhūr* and other [vyāhṛtis], having presented the internal *bali*, and having sipped water (*ācamya*), he should enter within, circumambulate [the deity], prostrate, and inform Śiva: "O Lord, whether through knowledge or ignorance, whatever ritual action has been performed by me in this sacrifice— whether of body, speech, or mind— may it be accepted."

Having made this request—"May all of that, both yours and mine, be fulfilled through your grace"—the king or the official in charge should then offer everything, from gold and villages down to male and female slaves, for the sake of worship and for the purpose of dance, song, and so forth, to Mukkeśvara. Any person other than the king should offer a sixth part of their own wealth. Then, having gone near the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*), one should perform a hundred oblations at a time with the *Aghora* mantra and the sword-mantra of Śiva.

One should offer oblations separately with the *mūla-mantras* of the Śiva-weapon, Aghora-weapon, and Pāśupata-weapon, as well as with the Sāvitrī, Gāyatrī, and Pratyaṅgirā mantras, in numbers of one thousand, five hundred, one hundred, or twenty-eight. Then, with the Vāgīśvarī mantra, one should offer one thousand, one hundred, or [the number] accompanied by a full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*). Following that—having established two jars on the eastern side of the altar in the manner of the Śiva-jar and having worshipped them—one should go near the Śiva[-liṅga] and present the oblation.

Having worshipped Śiva with the Gāyatrī mantra, one should then go near the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) and offer seven oblations beginning with "Stira" for the sake of completing the rite: *oṃ śiva sthiro bhava svāhā*; *oṃ śiva aprameyo bhava svāhā*; *oṃ śiva anādibodho bhava svāhā*; *oṃ śiva nityo bhava svāhā*; *oṃ śiva vyāpako bhava svāhā*; *oṃ śiva avinaśvaro bhava svāhā*; *oṃ śiva tṛpto bhava svāhā*.

Thus one should offer seven oblations. To complete what has been done or left undone, one should again offer a thousand, or five hundred, or a hundred oblations with the *aghora* mantra, accompanied by the sword-mantra (*asi*) and the *śiva*-mantra, together with the final full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*). Then, having offered betel and other items to the deity residing in the fire, and having worshipped him with the eightfold flower-offering (*aṣṭapuṣpikā*), and having presented the *arghya*, one should unite the deity residing in the fire with the *śiva*-vessel (*śivakumbha*). Having performed the oblations with the *bhūḥ* and other mantras, and having made the inner and outer offerings (*balis*), one should also unite the deity situated on the sacrificial mound (*sthaṇḍila*) with the vessel.

Having performed the ten gifts, beginning with the gift of a cow (*godāna*), one should unite even the [water] contained in the pitcher with the auspicious *liṅga*. Having bathed the auspicious [liṅga] with each of the pitchers placed in the pitcher[-stand], and having consecrated the pitchers of the Vidyeśvaras and others with their respective mantras in their respective places, one should then adorn Śiva with perfumes, garlands, and so forth. Having performed the installation of the vital breaths (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*) and the placement of the life-force (*jīvan nyāsa*), [one recites]: "Oṃ; for the mantra of the installation of the vital breaths, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara are the seers (*ṛṣi*)."

The deity is the Supreme Power (*parā-śakti*), the cause of the creation of the entire universe, who is established as the vital breath (*prāṇa-pratiṣṭhā*) within the *Ṛg*, *Yajur*, *Sāman*, and *Atharva* Vedas along with their meters. *Āṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), *Krauṃ* is the power (*śakti*); the application (*viniyoga*) is for the purpose of establishing the vital breath of the mantra. The visualization (*dhyāna*):
She stands upon a multitude of red lotuses shining in a blood-red ocean filled with water;
with her lotus-like hands she holds a noose, a bow made of sugarcane, a rosary of *rudrākṣa* beads, a goad, and the five arrows.

May the Goddess Prāṇaśakti— who possesses quivering temples and is enriched by full breasts, whose complexion resembles the radiance of the rising sun, and who is superior to all else— be for our protection.

Oṃ hāṃ hrīṃ krauṃ ya ra la va śa ṣa sa ha so’haṃ haṃ saḥ. O Great Breath of this person, Oṃ āṃ hrīṃ krauṃ ya ra la va śa ṣa sa haḥ so’haṃ haṃ saḥ. The life-force (*jīva*) of this person is stationed here: āṃ hrīṃ krauṃ ya ra la va śa ṣa sa haḥ sauṃ haṃ haṃ saḥ. May all the three—speech, mind, sight, hearing, tongue, nose, skin, flesh, blood, marrow, bone, and semen—of this person come right here; having come right here, [remain].

May they remain here in happiness for a long time: *Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Haṃ Saḥ So’haṃ Saḥ So’haṃsa Svāhā*. *Āṃ Kroṃ Ya Ra La Va Śa Ṣa Sa Ha So’haṃ Saḥ Āṃ Iṃ Vaṃ Gaṃ Ghaṃ Kaṃ*. From space comes air, from fire comes water, to the self of earth: *Aḥ Hṛdayāya Namaḥ*. *Āṃ Krīṃ Ya Ra La Va Śa Ṣa Sa Ha So’haṃ Īm Jñaṃ Jhaṃ Jaṃ Chaṃ Caṃ*. To the self of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell: *Maṃ Śirase Svāhā*.

Āṃ krīṃ kroṃ ya ra la va śa ṣa sa ha so’haṃ haṃ saḥ uṃ ūṃ ḍhaṃ ḍaṃ ṭhaṃ ṭaṃ, to the self of the ear, skin, eye, flesh, blood, marrow, bone, and semen; uṃ, to the crest-lock (śikhā), vauṣaṭ! Āṃ krīṃ kroṃ ya ra la va śa ṣa sa ha so’haṃ haṃ saḥ aiṃ naṃ dhaṃ daṃ thaṃ taṃ, to the self of speech, feet, hands, anus, and generative organ; aiṃ, to the armor (kavaca), hūṃ!

Āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ hrīṃ kroṃ ya ra la va śa ṣa sa ha so’haṃ haṃ saḥ oṃ maṃ bhaṃ baṃ phaṃ paṃ, to the Self consisting of speech, movement, giving, emission, and bliss: oṃ to the three eyes, vauṣaṭ! Āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ ya ra la va śa ṣa sa haḥ so’haṃ haṃ saḥ.

Aṃ kṣaṃ laṃ haṃ saḥ | Ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ | Ṣaṃ saḥ | So'haṃ haṃ saḥ | To the self consisting of the speech, mind, eyes, ears, tongue, nose, intellect, ego, and consciousness of all the senses of this [person], Aṃ, to the weapon, Phaṭ! This is the Sarvapratiṣṭhānyāsa.

Oṃ āṃ kroṃ oṃ hāṃ hauṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ ḷaṃ kṣaṃ. Oṃ, the vital breath (*prāṇa*) of such-and-such a person is here; the life-force (*jīva*) of such-and-such a person is stationed here. May all the senses, speech, mind, and bodily actions—along with hearing, touch, sight, taste, and smell—of such-and-such a person come here and remain for a long time in happiness. Bring all the worlds under my control, svāhā! Oṃ kaṃ, the syllable *iṃ*, to the one who pervades space (*vyomavyāpin*). Thus is the ten-syllable ritual placement (*nyāsa*), situated upon the Brahma-Kūrma seat.
The first seed-syllable is Oṃkāra, while Haṃkāra is the second;
the third seed-syllable is Ūkāra, the cause of all causes.
The fourth seed-syllable is *maṃ*; the fifth should be *oṃ*.
The sixth would be *a*, and likewise the seventh is *va*.
The eighth seed-syllable is *sa*, and the ninth is known to be *na*.
The syllable *oṃ* is the tenth seed-syllable, renowned as the self of all.

The life-breath of that person is here; the life-force of that person is established here. All the senses of that person—speech, mind, hearing, touch, sight, taste, and smell—are right here. Svāhā to each sense! Thus ends the *Prāṇapratiṣṭhā*, the supreme secret from the dialogue between the manifest and the unmanifest. Hariḥ Om.
The Jīvanyāsa:

Oṃ, salutations to Śiva, the source of all, who pervades the sky, whose form is the void, who pervades everything, who is infinite, who has no protector, who is without support, who is firm, eternal, the eternally united one, the one who draws away [the mind] through meditation; Oṃ, salutations, salutations to Śiva. [Salutations] to the one whose head is Īśāna, whose face is Tatpuruṣa, whose heart is Aghora, whose secret part is Vāmadeva, and whose form is Sadyojāta; Oṃ, salutations, salutations.

To the one more secret than the secret, the protector, the non-end of ends, the source of the end, the presiding authority over all yoga, the supreme among all sciences, whose form is light, who is devoted to the Supreme Lord; O conscious and unconscious one, O sky, O sky, O pervasive one, O pervasive one, O formless one, O having form, O primordial one, O primordial one, O splendor, O splendor, O light, O light, O formless one, O having form, O fire without smoke or ash, O unattained, O unattained, O manifold, O manifold, dhū-dhū dhū-dhū! Oṃ bhūḥ! Oṃ bhuvaḥ! Oṃ suvaḥ!

Oṃ! O you who are without end, born from the end; O bestower of happiness to all beings; O supreme one present in all; O you who transcend Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, and Ananta; O worshipped and unworshipped; O praised and formerly praised; O formerly established; O witness; O witness! Turu turu! O Pataṅga, Pataṅga; Piṅga, Piṅga; O Knowledge, Knowledge; O Sound, Sound; O Subtle, Subtle; O Śiva, Śarva! Oṃ, obeisance to Śiva! Oṃ, obeisance, obeisance!

Oṃ aṃ uṃ oṃ gaṃ saṃ raṃ, obeisance to Brahma-Īśa. [Place] at the secret place (*guhya*). Śiṃ, obeisance to Rudra. [Place] at the belly (*udara*). Maṃ, obeisance to Viṣṇu. [Place] at the navel (*nābhi*). Vaṃ, obeisance to Parāśakti. [Place] at the forehead (*lalāṭa*). Yaṃ, [obeisance] to Tāṇḍava-Sadāśiva. [Place] at the aperture (*randhra*). Niṃ is the binding of the directions (*digbandhana*). One should display the *dhenumudrā*. Namaśśivāya. Naṃ maṃ śiṃ vāṃ yaṃ—these are the five syllables. Oṃ naṃ, obeisance to Earth (*pṛthivī*). [Place] on the left arm. Oṃ maṃ, obeisance to Water (*ap*). [Place] on the right arm.

On the left arm: *oṃ śiṃ analāya namaḥ*. At the heart: *oṃ vaṃ vāyave namaḥ*. At the mouth: *oṃ yaṃ ākāśāya namaḥ*. On the head: thus one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) with the thumb and forefinger joined.
One should place the letter *a* on the head and the letter *ā* on the forehead;
the letter *i* on the right eye and the letter *ī* on the left eye.
The letter *u* is in the right ear, and the letter *ū* is in the left ear;
the letter *ṛ* is in the right nostril, and the letter *ṝ* is in the left nostril;
the letter *ḷ* is in the right ear, and the letter *ḹ* is in the left ear.
One should assign *e* and *ai* to the two lips, and *o* and *au* to the two rows of teeth as well.
One should place *aṃ* at the root of the palate and *aḥ* in front of the tip [of the tongue] in sequence;
the *ka*-group on the right hand and the *ca*-group on the left hand.
The *ṭa*-group [of consonants] is on the right foot; the *ta*-group is on the left feet. *Pa* and *pha* are on the right side, while *ba* and *bha* are on the left side.
*Ma* is on the right hip, and *ya* is on the left hip.
One should place *raṃ* and *laṃ* at the region of the hips, and the syllable *va* on the waistband.
One should place the letter Śa and the letter Ṣa upon the earrings;
one should assign the letter Sa to the heart and assign the letter Ha to the crown. One should place the letter La at the region of the genitals and the letter Kṣa at the region of the navel.

The internal *mātṛkā*: *oṃ hāṃ sadāśivātmane namaḥ*—the face. *oṃ rudrātmane namaḥ*—the heart. *oṃ viṣṇvātmane namaḥ*—the belly. *oṃ brahmaṇe namaḥ*—the feet. *oṃ candramaṇḍalāya namaḥ*—the mouth. *oṃ ādityamaṇḍalāya namaḥ*—the chest. *oṃ hāṃ haṃ agnimaṇḍalāya namaḥ*—the navel. Having recited the *yaśakti* mantra and performed worship ending with the offering of food (*naivedya*), incense, and lamps, one should worship with abundant offerings.

Then, having gone to the vicinity of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) and dismissed the fire, having dismissed the pitchers of the world-protectors (*lokapāla*) and so forth, having dismissed the pavilion by throwing water upwards from his own hand, having performed the ritual sipping of water (*ācamana*), having performed the ritual of total identification (*sakalīkaraṇa*), having gone into the presence of Śiva, having offered up the ritual action (*karman*), having announced the completion of the rite, and having given the sacrificial offering (*bali*) to Rudra and the others; then, having prepared two mandalas in the southern direction of his own [space] (the inner *antarbali*).

In the first maṇḍala, in the directions from the east to the north: *oṃ hāṃ rudrebhyo namaḥ*; *oṃ hāṃ mātṛbhyo namaḥ*; *oṃ hāṃ gaṇebhyo namaḥ*; *oṃ hāṃ yakṣebhyo namaḥ*. In the intermediate corners starting from the northeast (*īśāna*): *oṃ hāṃ gṛhebhyo namaḥ*; *oṃ hāṃ asurebhyo namaḥ*; *oṃ hāṃ rākṣasebhyo namaḥ*; *oṃ hāṃ nāgebhyo namaḥ*. In the center of the maṇḍala, in the northeast, southeast (*āgneya*), and southwest (*naiṛta*): *oṃ hāṃ nakṣatrebhyo namaḥ*; *oṃ hāṃ rāśibhyo namaḥ*.

Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Viśvedevas. Between Vāyu and Varuṇa: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Kṣetrapāla.
